overview.text: The Indian (Common) Wolf Snake is a non-venomous snake of South Asia and one of the commonest snakes in India and Sri Lanka. It is often confused with the venomous Common Krait, which it resembles.

identification.text: Colour varies. It can be told from a krait by a small scale (the loreal) between the eye and nostril, which kraits lack.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Pakistan, India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Myanmar and the Maldives.

behaviour.text: Active at night. If it cannot escape it defends itself fiercely and can bite hard, but it is not venomous.

reproduction.text: Lays 8 to 16 long eggs in small bunches.

recognise.text: Looks like a krait but has a loreal scale.
